title: Configuration, Profiles and Agent Anatomy
summary: Profiles, module toggles, and how configuration resolves

lessons.title: Profiles
lessons.body: A profile is a named bundle of Nerve module settings under HERMES_HOME/nerve/profile.json plus per-profile state. Named profiles (operator, lean, legacy...) change module counts; existing profiles keep their identity until migrated.

lessons.title: Config resolution
lessons.body: Settings resolve env -> config.yaml -> profile advanced -> defaults. The plugin registers the effective values at startup.

lessons.title: Module anatomy
lessons.body: Modules: gate (HITL), nervous (supervision), experience, selective context, reflex providers, work, context engine, receipts, ledger.

lab.goal: Initialize a sandbox profile and read back the effective module set.
steps: cd nerve-v0.4.0 && PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 -c "from hermes_nerve import profiles; print(profiles.list_profiles())"
Create a scratch HERMES_HOME and initialize the operator profile through the CLI.
Print the resolved config and count enabled modules.
lab.expect: You can explain why an existing Legacy profile does not silently gain modules.

task.intro: Answer the scenario questions; the engine verifies them deterministically in a disposable fixture. Your answers are never executed as commands.

questions.q: Which file overrides config.yaml for profile settings?
questions.why: The profile sidecar at $HERMES_HOME/nerve/profile.json takes precedence.

questions.q: Which profile is default for NEW installs? (operator/legacy)
questions.why: New setups default to Operator; existing Legacy stays Legacy.

questions.q: What must exist before changing a profile? (backup/rollback/either)
questions.why: A restorable backup/rollback point is required before profile changes.

executable.task: Produce a profile-change plan with precedence and rollback specifics.

check.question: Q: Which profile is applied to newly initialized installs by default?

troubleshooting: Module counts are exact per profile - do not hand-edit profile.json; use the CLI.
